name: Harold Bloodworth
bio: 'Pug' of George Ives's household - a working-class former footballer who joined in 1909, outlived Ives, and inherited the Adelaide Road house jointly with 'Elephant'. Cook records Ives's diary grief when Pug was away, and his paternal framing of the household as his 'children'.
bio_sources: Cook, London and the Culture of Homosexuality (2003), p. 148
bio_note: Footballer identity, survival of Ives and the joint inheritance from Cook 2014 printed p. 96 (repo PDF 107, folio confirmed); the diary passage on sleeping beside Pug and Cubby at printed p. 101 (repo PDF 112, folio confirmed); both read as page images 2026-08-03. The 1909 move-in is from Cook 2003 p. 148. Birth and death dates not established in the works read. DATES: NOT FOUND; RECORDED AS UNRECOVERED (2026-08-03). Cook names him at printed pp. 96, 109 and 110 (repo PDF 107, 120, 121) - footballer, joined the household, outlived Ives, inherited jointly, executor of the will, 'had lived with Ives at this point for around 30 years' - and attaches no dates to him anywhere. Searched so far, WITHOUT RESULT: Cook, Queer Domesticities (2014), repo PDF - every occurrence of the surname in the whole book, plus the endnotes and bibliography for the household chapter; the Ives repo transcripts (ives_diaries_burnet.txt, ives_letters_burnet_collated.txt, ives_letters_burnet_transcription.txt, ives_lewis_correspondence_2026-06.md), which contain no occurrence of any of the household surnames; and the open web, which returned only the Palgrave chapter version of Cook's same text ('George Ives, Queer Lives and the Family') and no dates. Cook is the only scholar to have written this household up and he dates their arrivals, their departures and Ives's will, but never a person: he gives no birth or death date for any member of the household. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT: census, GRO index and probate research on common English surnames - work so far could not do. Ives's own proved will (Cook, printed pp. 109-110), which leaves the Adelaide Road house to Bloodworth and Saunders, names Bloodworth an executor and portions the Goddards, is the natural documentary starting point, since a grant of probate fixes addresses and often identifies legatees.
